Where I got to
I reconstructed your working tree from dump.txt and verified it: 344 of 344 files match their recorded SHA-256 (the only two that needed repair were artefacts of my parser, not of your export — export.sh contains its own # FILE: banner as literal text, and the last file in the dump abuts the DUMP SUMMARY footer). So I'm working against a byte-exact copy of b274d5f.

The four build errors are one defect, not four
All four come from the same collision, and it is a Razor parser reserved word rather than anything wrong with your markup:

File	Line	Text
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Components/Pages/Administration/CreateMenuItem.razor	125	<option value="@section.MenuSectionIdentifier">
src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Components/Pages/Table/TableOrderSurface.razor	223	@section.MenuSectionName
@section is the MVC section directive. The Razor parser sees @section and tries to read a directive name after it, which is why the errors read RZ2005 'section' directive must appear at the start of the line and RZ1011 'section' directives value(s) must be separated by whitespace — RZ1011's column (41 / 41) lands exactly on the . immediately after the seven characters of section. Both loop variables are named section; @key="section.…" and @SectionHeadingId(section) on the neighbouring lines compile fine because they are not preceded by @.

Grep across the tree confirms these are the only two occurrences — every other section in a .razor file is an HTML <section> tag.

The fix is to rename the two loop variables (e.g. menuSection), which is why full files matter here: the identifier appears on several lines in TableOrderSurface.razor and a partial rename would compile into a different error. I also noticed the inner @foreach in TableOrderSurface.razor (lines 227–250) was never re-indented when Slice 40 wrapped it in the outer grouping loop, so it sits four levels shallow inside its parent — worth correcting in the same pass since the file is being rewritten whole.

Per your F-47 habit, this wants a rule rather than a memory: no .razor file may contain the token @section. This project uses no Razor sections anywhere (that's an MVC feature; Blazor has none), so the rule is total, decidable from text, and would have failed at unit-test time instead of at dotnet build. That belongs beside the existing scans in tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/Components/, and it earns a finding number — F-81.

What I had loaded for the menu work when the tool budget ran out
I'd read the full Stage 3 plan and the surrounding code, and the shape of the next slice is clear. The section editor is the single highest-value item left, and it is what unblocks four other deferred things at once:

IMenuSectionEventLog does not exist — there is MenuEventLog.cs for items and no counterpart for menu_section_event, so §11.4's "complete uncapped event history at the bottom" has nothing to read from.
Four IMenuSectionAdministration verbs (Rename, Describe, Reorder, SetMenuSectionActive) are still outside IMenuWorkflow, and MenuWiringTests.FakeMenuSectionAdministration throws from all four with a message pointing at the plan — so wiring them in is a deliberate red until the fakes and facts land with them.
AdministrationJourneys.CreateMenuSectionAsync currently recovers the new identifier from the item form's <option value> because a section has no manage page to link to. That shape goes away with the editor.
Scenario 17's cut assertion (deactivate a heading → it vanishes from the guest's menu) becomes reachable, closing the one §7 asymmetry that is currently unverified end to end.
What I need from you before continuing
I have the tree and the plan; what I don't have is your call on scope, and this is a veto-protocol decision rather than something I should just pick:

Option A — errors only. Fix F-81 in both Razor files, add the @section contract assertion, ledger row, §16.4 paragraph, changelog. Small, certainly green, no menu progress.

Option B — errors + section editor (my recommendation). All of A, plus ManageMenuSection.razor at /administration/menu/sections/{id}, IMenuSectionEventLog + DapperMenuSectionEventLog, the four workflow verbs with their §9 broadcasts, MenuWiringTests facts for each, MenuSectionEventLogTests, the harness journey rewritten to read the "Manage this section" link, and scenario 17's deactivation assertion restored. That is one slice by your atomic rule because the verbs, the surface and the fake all have to move together — same argument 0005 made.

Option C — B plus MoveMenuItemToSectionAsync and the section picker on ManageMenuItem. Larger; I'd rather land B first and take the move verb next, since it has its own migration-free but event-shaped questions.

Tell me A, B, or C and I'll deliver the structured .tar.gz extractable at the repo root, full files only, with the explicit "Files to DELETE" section (empty or not), git add reminders for new paths, BUILD_PROGRESS.md whole, and the predicted test count flagged as uncompiled arithmetic off the current ~1136.

A second red gate, hidden behind the first
While wiring up TestingSectionContractTests I simulated it against your tree as delivered. It fails now, before any of my changes:
